title: edge-cache-eviction-cost-model-and-sales-faq
content:
Purpose:
This doc bundles an engineer-friendly eviction cost model for edge/local-region caches tied to region-pinning, plus a lightweight sales FAQ and operator checklist. Aim: give sales and onboarding a quick, defensible answer about why we sometimes evict tenant anchors, what the economics look like, and how we mitigate customer impact.

Background and context (tl;dr):
- Private deployments often use edge caches (regional KV prefix + pinned tenant anchors) to reduce cross-region egress and speed up cold-start tokens.
- When capacity is constrained or a tenant's anchor is idle, edge caches may evict KV entries or soft-pin anchors to free memory. Eviction is a key lever for cost/efficiency but common source of customer questions.
- This doc assumes: billing for Dedicated/private includes reserved GPU pool + regional object store + edge RAM costs; customers expect determinism for "pinned" region but accept limited soft-eviction during bursts if negotiated.

Eviction patterns defined here:
- soft-evict (preferred): demote tenant anchor from memory, keep compressed shard on local disk for fast reload (100-400ms reload target).
- hard-evict: remove all local artifacts, reload from anchor region over network (1.2s-6s depending on model + network).
- spill-to-secondary-region: if anchored region overloaded, route new work to a secondary pinned region (used only for non-regulatory workloads).

Simple cost model (per-tenant, monthly) - assumptions + example numbers (ballpark for sales):
- average anchor RAM per active tenant: 6 GB (LLM KV + session state)
- local-cache storage: $0.15/GB-month for NVMe (on-prem pricing varies)
- RAM cost (reserved): $4.50/GB-month (amortized across pools)
- network egress penalty on hard-evict reload: 120 ms per request peak + 50 GB/month extra egress -> ~$6/month egress
- operator overhead / margin: $8/month per tenant (monitoring, guardrails)

Model: incremental monthly cost to avoid eviction = RAM_cost * anchor_RAM + storage_cost * local_disk_copy + margin
Example: keep anchor in RAM to avoid hard-evict:
- RAM: 6 GB * $4.50 = $27.00/month
- local storage (for snapshot): 6 GB * $0.15 = $0.90/month
- margin/ops: $8.00/month
Total incremental cost to guarantee in-RAM pin: ~$35.90/month/tenant

Interpretation and negotiation levers for sales:
- If a customer values <200ms cold-start SLO, recommend dedicated-reserved anchors (add-on priced by anchors * $36/mo).
- For cost-sensitive customers, propose soft-pin with guaranteed reload 400ms SLAs; cheaper because archival copy is local disk not RAM (price ~ $10–12/mo).
- For regulatory sovereign customers who require region-only serving, present hard-pin SLA (no spill-to-secondary) with higher price to cover spare capacity.

Sales FAQ (short answers to common Qs)
Q: Why did my model slow down after midnight?
A: Edge pools perform periodic reclaim to balance tenant memory. If your tenant was idle, we may have soft-evicted the anchor to free RAM. You can opt into an "always-warm" anchor to avoid this (see pricing note above).

Q: Will eviction move my data out of the contracted region?
A: No. All eviction mechanics respect the tenant's region pin. Soft-evict keeps a local disk snapshot in the same region; hard-evict reloads from the same anchored region. We never move residency without an explicit migration.

Q: What is the user-visible impact of soft vs hard eviction?
A: Soft-evict: first request after idle may see ~100–400ms extra latency. Hard-evict: first request can see 1–6s extra depending on model size and network. Subsequent requests are back to baseline.

Q: How do you ensure compliance for sovereign customers?
A: For sovereign/private deployments we support: (a) hard-region-lock (no cross-region reload allowed), (b) HSM/KMS controls for keys restricted to region, (c) audit logs that show anchor load/unload events with region tags.

Operator checklist (implementation and runbook notes):
- Pre-deploy: add tenant to anchor-catalog with fields: tenant_id, region_pin, anchor_tier (soft/hard/always-warm), expected_rps, sla_latency_target.
- Sizing: compute pool RAM budget = sum(anchors.always_warm * anchor_RAM) + 20% buffer for burst.
- Eviction policy flags (runtime knobs):
  * eviction.threshold.memory_percent (default 72%)
  * eviction.soft_ttl.idle_seconds (default 3600)
  * eviction.hard_grace.period (default 300)
  * eviction.reload_rate_limit.per_minute (default 120)
- Typical ops commands (examples):
  * list anchors in pool: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://private-api.internal/anchors?pool=europe-west1
  * force warm anchor (operator): POST /anchors/:id/retain -d '{"duration":3600}'
  * telemetry: query redis: TS.RANGE anchor:loads - + FILTER tenant_id
- Runbook: on spike-induced evictions -> 1) set temporary retain for top-affected tenants, 2) scale up autoscaling GPU nodes via /autoscale endpoint, 3) notify SRE channel with postmortem ticket.

Telemetry & dashboards to monitor (KPIs):
- anchor_eviction_rate (per-pool, 1h / 24h)
- average_reload_latency_first_request (p50/p95/p99)
- eviction-induced_error_rate (errors correlated with reloads)
- memory_headroom_percent (per-region pool)
- cost_per_anchor_monthly (rolling)

Open questions and TODOs (for engineering + product):
- Q1: define standard measurement for "reload latency" across different models (sampler vs autoreg). Need test harness (see PROJ-4821).
- Q2: consider a mid-tier product: "burst-warm" anchors that are warm during business hours only (pricing model and contract language needed).
- Q3: flesh out legal wording for "soft-eviction" impact in enterprise contracts—ops should provide deterministic max-first-request latency.

Appendix: negotiation script snippets for SDRs/AE
- If price pushback: "We can reduce cost by switching to soft-pin; expected first-request latency for soft-pin is ~300ms and we cap it in the contract. If you need stricter guarantees, the always-warm add-on ensures sub-50ms cold-starts at $X/anchor."
- If compliance pushback: "We support region locks and provide full audit evidence (anchor load/unload events, storage proofs). We can schedule a joint runbook review with SRE to map your compliance controls to our telemetry."

References and links:
- PROJ-4821: reload-latency-harness (Jira)
- runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298 (eviction knobs + metrics)
- Confluence: region-pin-telemetry-hub
- Slack: #private-deploys thread "CACHED-eviction-questions"

Notes to self (rough):
- Need a small benchmark matrix (gpt-like-7B, 13B, 70B) for soft vs hard reloads, ideally automated in the next sprint.
- Confirm with finance whether the per-anchor margin should be $8 or $12 (affects pricing).
- Next steps: convert top sections into a one-pager for AE playbook and a short FAQ page in the customer onboarding kit.

-- end --
